evidence: Cic. Off. 3.35: rēcta et convenientia et cōnstantia nātūra dēsīderat (Lewis & Short, s.v. conveniō)
terms.comment: Of a person or a course of action that stays the same; cōnstantia is consistency. It also means firm, steadfast.

terms.gloss: to be consistent, stay true to oneself
terms.grammar: phrase: cōnstō, cōnstāre with the dative of the reflexive
terms.comment: “To agree with oneself”: of a person, a speech or an argument. The adverb cōnstanter is “consistently”.
Even, the same throughout; aequābilitās, evenness of life and conduct, is Cicero’s word.

phrases.latin: omnīnō sī quicquam est decōrum, nihil est profectō magis quam aequābilitās ūniversae vītae
phrases.english: if anything at all is becoming, nothing surely is more so than consistency in the whole of one’s life

phrases.latin: in Oppiānicō sibi cōnstāre et superiōribus cōnsentīre jūdiciīs dēbuērunt
phrases.english: in the case of Oppianicus they ought to have been consistent with themselves and agreed with the earlier verdicts

sources: Lewis & Short: consto · Lewis & Short: aequabilis · Lewis & Short: decorus
